prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0044: TGUIs can be configured to display trial plan impacts on schedules to both Arrival Group (MFs, runways) and EDC Group (XMPs, CMPs) metering points and may reside in either the ‘home’ ARTCC TMU or the adjacent facility TMU (if desired and as needed).
U0045: The DRAW system utilizes current and forecasted convective weather data to calculate polygon-based weather avoidance fields.
U0046: DRAW currently uses MIT Lincoln Labs developed Corridor Integrated Weather System (CIWS) and Convective Weather Avoidance Model (CWAM) for convective weather data and weather avoidance polygons, respectively[5].
U0047: However, other convective weather models could be used by DRAW so long as the resulting weather avoidance fields are represented by polygons.
U0048: DRAW combines a Center-based trajectory to the meter fix with a TRACON trajectory, such as the one developed for Terminal Sequencing and Spacing (TSAS), to give full weather detection coverage from en route airspace to runway.
U0049: An example of DRAW’s trajectory-based weather detection capability and forecasted convective weather models is shown in Figure 4.
U0050: Two weather products are displayed: current weather and forecast weather.
U0051: Figure 4 shows current weather (thin, nested contours indicating severity) provided by the CIWS.
U0052: When the TMC uses the trial planner capability, DRAW detects and highlights forecasted weather conflicts and nearby convective weather avoidance polygons corresponding to the flight’s predicted time along the trajectory.
U0053: Weather avoidance polygons are derived from weather forecasts to model regions that flights should avoid when considering a reroute.
U0054: The weather avoidance fields (WAFs) in Figure 4 (bold yellow and cyan polygons) are derived from CIWS forecast data by CWAM and represent the regions that 70% of pilots are likely to avoid.
U0055: Note: Weather polygons are only displayed during trial planning but not when DRAW’s rerouting algorithm is analyzing trajectories for conflicts internally.
U0056: Figure 4: Trajectory-Based Weather Modeling 4.2 DRAW ROUTE ADVISORY TYPES The DRAW routing algorithm continuously analyzes flight trajectories for opportunities to improve arrival traffic flow.
U0057: Arrival trajectories are analyzed to determine if they meet criteria that would trigger DRAW to generate one of two types of DRAW route advisories, time-saving routes to alternate meter fixes and route corrections to avoid weather.
U0058: DRAW route advisories are calculated for individual flights and for groups of flights when the specified criteria are met.
U0059: The trial planner may also be used to manually create a route at any point including inside of the freeze horizon. 4.2.1 Time-Saving Routes to Alternate Meter Fixes Section 2.1 describes the problem of inefficient or obsolete weather avoidance routes.
U0060: In these situations, the weather may move or not materialize as predicted, thus providing an opportunity to reroute flights to save time.
U0061: For each arrival flight, DRAW searches for time- savings opportunities by comparing the flight’s current flight plan trajectory with a series of trajectories along STARs to alternate meter fixes and STAR transitions.
U0062: If time-savings is in excess of the user defined threshold (e.g., 5 minutes), a DRAW route advisory will be triggered.
U0063: In the example shown in Figure 5, STARs to Meter Fix 1 (MF1) were originally blocked by weather, causing flights to file less efficient southerly routes to Meter Fix 2 (MF2, shown in green).
U0064: DRAW analyzes more direct routes available to MF1 and triggers route advisories for multiple flights (AC4 and AC5) that save 5 minutes or more in flight time due to weather movement away from Meter Fix 1.
U0065: The proposed DRAW routes and their corresponding metering impacts are shown in magenta.
U0066: Figure 5: DRAW Time-Saving Routes 4.2.2 Route Corrections to Avoid Weather DRAW provides reroutes advisories intended to help sustain metering operations in the presence of weather.
U0067: A notional example illustrating a DRAW reroute for weather is shown in Figure 6.
U0068: The current flight plan of AC1, shown on the left in green, is predicted to conflict with weather.
U0069: A simplified TGUI timeline for Meter Fix 1 (MF1), on the right in Figure 6, shows the current times of arrival for AC1, as well as AC2, in green.
U0070: These STAs are based on the current flight plans, and do not reflect the need to deviate around weather.
U0071: As a result, these STAs are outdated and cannot be used for metering.
